_comment: Where hipointe-demun's data wells are. Shape: cartograph/sources.js.
_why_two_wells: HiPointe–DeMun STRADDLES the City limit: Hi-Pointe is in St. Louis City, DeMun is in St. Louis County / City of Clayton. St. Louis City is an independent city, so its assessor holds no County parcels — two wells, complementary, and a field is absent for this scene only if BOTH lack it (which is why num_buildings/vacant/historic_district survive here on the city side).

parcels.attribution: City of St. Louis Assessor — Assessor_Public_Parcels
parcels._note: St. Louis City is an INDEPENDENT CITY — its assessor holds only City parcels. The historical acquisition is scripts/03-fetch-stl-parcels.py, which also folds AprComImprove into appraised_value, LastYearBuilt into year_built and NbrOfBldgsCom into num_buildings, and reads LocalHistDist/CertLocalHistDist. cartograph/fetch-parcels.mjs maps one column per field, so re-fetching through the button would lose those second operands. ⛔ The existing raw/stl_parcels.json is the Python script's output and must NOT be re-fetched through the button until the field map grows a fallback-column form. Declared here so the FILENAME hardcode could die; the endpoint is recorded, not yet exercised on this town.

parcels.attribution: St. Louis County OpenData — Tax Parcels
parcels._note: The SECOND well for a neighborhood that straddles the City limit — DeMun is in St. Louis County / City of Clayton. Same caveat as stl-city: raw/stlco_parcels.json is scripts/03b's output, the endpoint is recorded but not yet exercised through the generic button.

_landUseCodes_why: The county well's LUCODE is numeric and opaque; the CSV is the assessor's own decode table, published alongside the parcel layer and re-acquired per jurisdiction.
